chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: First New York band to use the conga permanently
summary: Cab Calloway used it on records, Cugat used it more permanently thanks to Miguelito Valdes.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Can you remember which was the first latin band in New York to utilize the conga drum?
The conga drum? Before we did, Xavier Cugat.
Xavier Cugat had the conga drum.
and before Xavier Cugat, Cab Calloway. Mario, one time, made a recording with 'Chile con Carne', another ....

No, no, what I am talking about is having it in the band as a permanent -- I know about Calloway. I know about 'Going Conga', 'Auto Conga,' those things he did in 1939, but he didn't always have it. He just used it for recording, right?
Who?
Calloway
Calloway, yes, for recording
Just for the recording.
Just for the recording.
I am talking about now, who was the first band leader in New York to use that as a permanent fixture in the band?
Xavier Cugat used it almost permanently because..
....because of Miguelito?
..because of Miguelito.
Macho, did you ever go to the Waldorf Astoria to see Miguelito Valdes while he performed with the Xavier Cugat band?
Yes
Did Miguelito used a conga drum then?
Yes.
Then, he was the first to bring the conga drum.
Absolutely
Okay. Do you know if he used it in his recording with Cugat?
Yes
He played conga, no one else.
No one else.
When he left Cugat's band in 1942, did Cugat keep the conga in the band?
In a way, yes.
Did he have anyone playing conga?
Yes, the bongo player used to double with the conga.
I see. Okay, so then is it safe to say that the Machito orchestra was the second band to use the conga drum?
Absolutely.
